predecessors.name: Bahmani Sultanate
predecessors.text: the Bahmani province around Junnar, where Malik Ahmad had been governor, and the lands the early sultans added to Daulatabad (1499)

successors.name: Mughal Empire
successors.text: the remnant of the Nizam Shahi state around Ahmadnagar, Junnar and Daulatabad

successors.name: Bijapur Sultanate
successors.text: Bijapur's share of the partition (undefined on the page)

ledger.x: 1490: Malik Ahmad Nizam Shah I declares independence from the Bahmani Sultanate at Junnar and founds the Nizam Shahi line.
1494: Ahmadnagar is founded and becomes the capital (infobox 'Ahmednagar (1494-1600)'; 'the new capital Ahmadnagar was founded in 1494').
c. 1540: two cells of the northern Konkan coast pass to the Portuguese in Cliopatria's shapes. No page opened dates it; the Portuguese Empire dossier should carry the matching gain.

c. 1547: Ahmadnagar's south-eastern frontier advances onto Bijapuri ground. The Adil Shahi page says Burhan Nizam Shah I 'besieged the Bijapuri city of Solapur four times, but did not retain it until a third invasion' and that Ali Adil Shah I's request for the return of Solapur and Kaliyani failed; no year is given…
c. 1552: the same strip reverts to Bijapur in Cliopatria's shapes; nothing on the pages opened dates the reversal (Kaliyani was returned in 1561, Solapur never).
1561: Hussain Nizam Shah I returns Kaliyani to Bijapur.
1574: Murtaza Nizam Shah I annexes Berar, taking Ahmadnagar to its greatest extent.
23 February 1596: Chand Bibi makes peace with the Mughal prince Murad by ceding Berar; 'she decided to make peace by ceding Berar to Murad, who retreated'.
23 February 1596: Berar passes to the Mughals.
1600: with Ahmadnagar lost, the Nizam Shahi court under Malik Ambar sits at Paranda (infobox 'Paranda (1600-1610)'); 'Malik Ambar backed Murtaza Nizam Shah II at Paranda'.
18 August 1600: Ahmadnagar falls to the Mughals.

1610: the capital moves to Khirki, the new city of Malik Ambar, later Aurangabad (infobox 'Aurangabad (1610-1636)', 'Junnar (1610)'; Malik Ambar page: 'He founded/inhabited the city of Khirki in 1610').
October 1636: Shahaji surrenders Mahuli and Junnar to the Mughals.
October 1636: the Nizam Shahi remnant is partitioned.
October 1636: the Ahmadnagar Sultanate ends, partitioned between the Mughal Empire and Bijapur.

wars.name: Battle of Talikota
wars.outcome: Victory of the Deccan sultanates; 'Rama Raya was beheaded by Sultan Nizam Hussain himself' (Ahmadnagar page); no transfer of territory to Ahmadnagar is listed.

wars.name: Mughal–Ahmadnagar conquest, 1595-1600
wars.outcome: Mughal victory: Berar ceded in February 1596; Ahmadnagar fort taken on 18 August 1600; Chand Bibi killed by her troops; the Nizam Shahi state survives as a remnant under Malik Ambar.

wars.name: Mughal conquest of the Ahmadnagar remnant, 1633-1636
wars.outcome: Mughal victory: Daulatabad falls in 1633; in 1636 the sultanate is partitioned between the Mughal Empire and Bijapur and Shahaji enters Bijapur's service.

certainty.note: No page opened gives a boundary line for Ahmadnagar; frontiers with Bijapur, Khandesh and Berar are Cliopatria's approximations.
